title: UN agencies warn humanitarian system in Sudan 'could collapse'
summary: UN aid agencies say they may be forced to drastically scale back operations in Sudan, now the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis, due to a lack of funding. An estimated 8.6 million people remain internally displaced and 19.5 million face severe food insecurity amid civil conflict that has continued since 2023.

title: Northern Nigeria's hunger crisis reaches levels not seen in nearly a decade
summary: Over 17 million people across nine conflict-affected northern Nigerian states now face Crisis-or-worse hunger levels. The World Food Programme says funding shortfalls have forced it to reach only 740,000 of the 6.2 million food-insecure people in three northeastern states, leaving millions more without support.

title: Haiti's displacement crisis nears 1.5 million amid escalating gang violence
summary: Gang violence has pushed displacement in Haiti to unprecedented levels, with roughly 1.5 million people now lacking stable shelter, according to the UN's migration agency. The crisis has spread beyond traditional conflict zones, and over 110,000 Haitians have been forcibly returned since early 2026, adding further pressure on strained services.

title: Drought keeps Kenya's pastoral regions in crisis through early 2027
summary: FEWS NET projects that 3.0 to 3.49 million people in Kenya's arid and semi-arid regions will need humanitarian food assistance between June 2026 and January 2027, with needs peaking in September and October. Conditions may ease in pastoral areas by October if the forecast above-average short rains arrive as expected.

title: Nearly half of government-controlled Yemen faces acute food insecurity
summary: New IPC analysis finds about 47%, roughly 5 million people, of the population in government-controlled areas of Yemen face Crisis-level or worse acute food insecurity, with conditions expected to worsen as humanitarian funding declines sharply. The assessment covers only government-held territory; comparable recent data for the Houthi-controlled north, home to most Yemenis, is not available.
